steps: Cook the brown rice according to package directions.
Slice the beef sirloin into thin strips against the grain.
Slice the bell pepper, cut the broccoli into small florets, trim the asparagus into short lengths, and mince the garlic and ginger.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat and sear the beef strips for 2 minutes, then set aside.
Stir-fry the broccoli for 2 minutes, then add the bell pepper and asparagus for a further 2 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the beef, add the soy sauce, season with salt and black pepper, and toss together.
Finish off the heat with the sesame oil and serve over the rice.

note: Sesame oil demoted from wok oil to finishing drizzle (5g->4g) and Vegetable Oil 8g added as the high-heat fat (report asked for Canola Oil, not in vocab; Vegetable Oil is its listed alternative, identical macros). Cauliflower dropped, broccoli 100->130 and bell pepper 80->90 to hold vegetable mass. Fresh Garlic+Ginger replace Garlic Powder. Steps re-sequenced so the florets get a head start and both remaining spices are named.

steps: Peel and cube the sweet potato, toss with the olive oil, and roast at 200°C (400°F) for 25 minutes.
Season the chicken breast with salt, black pepper, paprika, garlic powder and cayenne.
Grill or bake the chicken for 20-25 minutes until cooked through.
Brush the chicken with the BBQ sauce during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Toss the coleslaw mix with the mayonnaise and a splash of red wine vinegar to dress it.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, then serve with the roasted sweet potato and the slaw.

note: Phantom 'light dressing' resolved: Mayonnaise 15g added and the slaw is now actually dressed. Olive Oil 5g added so the sweet potato roasts in fat instead of dry. Garlic Powder and Cayenne are now named in step 2. Report's optional Apple Cider Vinegar is not in the frozen vocab, so Red Wine Vinegar (existing spice name, zero macros) stands in as the slaw acid. ~+145 cal / +16g fat as the report predicted.

steps: Use day-old cooked white rice for best results.
Dice the pork belly and render it in a hot dry wok until browned and the fat has run out, 3-4 minutes.
Add the diced carrot and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until it softens.
Push everything to one side, scramble the eggs in the rendered fat, and break them into small pieces.
Add the rice and green peas and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes, chopping to separate the grains.
Season with the soy sauce, salt and white pepper, and toss to combine.
Off the heat, stir through the sliced green onion and the sesame oil. Serve immediately.

note: Renamed Egg Fried Rice -> Pork Fried Rice: 70g of pork belly is a co-lead, not a garnish, so the old name was contradicted by its own ingredient list. Relabeled American -> Chinese. Green Onion 15g added (the dish's defining aromatic). Carrot moved from the final step to early so it actually cooks. Sesame oil 5g->3g and demoted to a finishing drizzle; no added cooking oil since the belly renders. Salt and White Pepper now named. Spices unchanged.

steps: Cook the brown rice according to package directions.
Trim the asparagus ends and toss with the olive oil, salt and black pepper.
Season the salmon with salt, black pepper and half the lemon juice.
Grill the salmon and asparagus, or roast them at 200°C (400°F), for 12-15 minutes.
Plate the brown rice, top with the salmon and asparagus, and drizzle the pesto sauce over the salmon.
Finish with the remaining lemon squeezed over.

note: Verdict was 'coherent' with no required fix; applied only the report's offered polish, both step-text-only and macro-neutral: the grill/roast instruction no longer reads as an oven temperature attached to grilling, and the 15g of lemon is now explicitly split between seasoning and finishing instead of being spent twice. Ingredients, spices and macros unchanged. Pesto Sauce retained per the nut-free-brand rule.

steps: Peel and cube the sweet potato, toss with the olive oil, salt and black pepper, and roast at 200°C (400°F) for 25 minutes.
Season the beef sirloin with salt and black pepper.
Sear the steak in a hot dry pan for 3-4 minutes per side for medium, adding the butter for the last minute and spooning it over the steak.
Let the steak rest for 5 minutes, then slice.
Steam the broccoli until tender-crisp, about 4 minutes, and season with salt and pepper.
Serve the sliced steak with the roasted sweet potato and broccoli.

note: Phantom-oil fix: step 1 tossed the sweet potato in oil the recipe did not contain, so Olive Oil 5g added. Butter kept at 10g but moved from the start of the sear to a last-minute baste, since its milk solids burn over a 3-4 min/side sear. Broccoli now seasoned. Spices unchanged. ~+44 cal / +5g fat.

steps: Use day-old cooked white rice for best results. Dice the chicken breast and mince the garlic.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat, cook the chicken until done, and set aside.
Scramble the egg in the wok and break it apart.
Add the minced garlic and the diced carrot and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the rice and green peas for a further 3-4 minutes, chopping to separate the grains.
Return the chicken, add the soy sauce, and season with salt and white pepper.
Off the heat, stir through the sliced green onion and the sesame oil. Serve immediately.

note: Relabeled American -> Chinese-American: the report called this the Chinese-American takeout configuration (diced chicken, frozen peas-and-carrots blend, egg, soy) and only settled for 'Chinese' because no Chinese-American label existed at audit time. Vegetable Oil 8g added as the wok fat (report wanted Canola Oil, not in vocab); sesame oil 5g->4g as a finishing drizzle. Green Onion 12g and Garlic 4g added as the missing aromatics. Salt and White Pepper now named in the steps. Spices unchanged.

steps: Soak the panko breadcrumbs in the whole milk for 5 minutes to make a panade.
Mix the ground beef with the soaked panko, the egg, the minced garlic, half the parmesan, salt, black pepper, oregano and dried basil. Form into meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in the olive oil on all sides.
Add the tomato sauce, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the meatballs are cooked through.
Spiralize or ribbon-cut the zucchini into zoodles.
Sauté the zoodles briefly in a hot pan for 2 minutes, then drain off the water they release.
Serve the meatballs and sauce over the zoodles with the remaining parmesan grated over.

note: Meatballs given a real panade and binder: Panko Breadcrumbs 15g + Whole Milk 15g + Egg 25g, plus Garlic 5g (the dish had no allium at all). Parmesan 15->20g, split half into the mix and half grated over. Zoodles now drained so the sauce does not puddle. Doubled conjunction in step 1 cleaned up. Spices unchanged (this recipe already named all four). ~+120 cal / +5g protein / +12g carb; low-carb tag kept, total carbs still ~27g. The 25g egg is a binder and the project's binder-egg cap is the desired behaviour here.

steps: Cook the white rice according to package directions.
Slice the beef sirloin thinly against the grain and toss it with half the cornstarch to velvet it.
Cut the broccoli into small florets and blanch for 2 minutes, then drain.
Stir the remaining cornstarch into the soy sauce with a splash of water to make a slurry.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat and sear the beef for 2 minutes, then set aside.
Mince the garlic and ginger, stir-fry them for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the blanched broccoli for 1-2 minutes.
Return the beef, pour in the slurry, and toss for 30-60 seconds until the sauce thickens and glosses. Season with salt and black pepper.
Finish off the heat with the sesame oil and serve over the rice.

note: Relabeled American -> Chinese-American, which the report named as the accurate label (Chinese-American adaptation of Cantonese gai lan chao niu rou) and only downgraded to 'Chinese' for lack of the label. Cornstarch 8g added — it does double duty as the velveting coat and the slurry that gives the dish its defining glossy clinging sauce. Fresh Garlic 6g + Ginger 5g replace Garlic Powder. Vegetable Oil 8g is the wok fat (report wanted Canola Oil, not in vocab); sesame oil 5g->4g as a finish. Broccoli now blanched so it is not raw in the stem. Oyster Sauce omitted — not in the frozen vocabulary, and per the report Hoisin Sauce must NOT be substituted. ~+105 cal.

steps: Cook the brown rice according to package directions and let it cool.
Peel and devein the shrimp. Sear in a little of the olive oil over high heat for 1-2 minutes per side until pink, then set aside to cool slightly.
Wash the spinach and slice the avocado.
Toss the spinach, brown rice, avocado and shrimp together.
Whisk the remaining olive oil with the juice of the lemon, dress the salad, and season with salt and black pepper.

note: Lemon 15g added — the dressing had no acid at all, and cooled brown rice plus avocado both need it. Olive Oil 10->12g so the sear has its own allocation instead of borrowing from a budget fully committed to dressing. Shrimp timing cut from 2-3 to 1-2 minutes per side and now cooled before it hits the raw spinach, so the salad does not wilt. Spices unchanged. Negligible macro change.

steps: Cook the brown rice according to package directions.
Slice the turkey breast into strips and mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a pan, season the turkey with salt and black pepper, and cook the strips for 2-3 minutes, turning once, until just golden and cooked through.
Steam or blanch the broccoli for 3-4 minutes until bright green.
Add the minced garlic and the soy sauce to the pan in the last 30 seconds and toss to coat the turkey.
Serve the turkey and broccoli over the rice.

note: Unused-ingredient fix: the garlic was minced in step 2 and then discarded — it now goes into the pan with the soy sauce. Turkey strip timing cut from 4-5 min per side (8-10 min total, which turns 160g of turkey breast to chalk) to 2-3 minutes total. Olive Oil 5g added; the bowl previously had zero added fat. Salt and Black Pepper now named. Spices unchanged. ~+44 cal / +5g fat.

steps: Peel and cube the sweet potato. Toss with about a third of the olive oil and roast at 200°C (400°F) for 20 minutes.
Mince the garlic and rub the chicken breast with it, plus salt and black pepper.
Pan-sear the chicken in a little more of the olive oil for 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through, then slice.
Dice the onion and sauté it in the remaining olive oil until softened and golden, 5-6 minutes, then add the spinach and wilt briefly.
Arrange the roasted sweet potato, the sliced chicken, and the onion and spinach in a bowl.

note: The onion was diced in step 4 and then abandoned, while step 6 served a 'sauteed onion' that never existed — it is now actually sautéed and plated, and the redundant final step is gone. Olive Oil 3->10g: 3g could not coat 120g of sweet potato, let alone also sear a 170g chicken breast and wilt the spinach. Garlic is now explicitly minced before being used as a rub. Spices unchanged. ~+62 cal / +7g fat.

_summary.notes: Pulled Pork Sandwich and Chipotle Chicken Bowl are NOT in this slice (they live in 01-american-breakfast-sandwiches and 04-mexican-bowls-burritos); no rebuild records emitted here and the 12-recipe count is unchanged. LABEL JUDGEMENT THE MERGE SHOULD KNOW: the report's 'Cuisine label' lines say `Chinese` for all three relabels, but only because no `Chinese-American` label existed at audit time — its prose explicitly identifies Chicken Fried Rice as the Chinese-American takeout configuration and Beef & Broccoli as the Chinese-American adaptation of gai lan chao niu rou, and names `Chinese-American` as more accurate. SPEC approves that label, so both use it; Pork Fried Rice stays `Chinese` because the report contrasts it as genuinely Chinese home cooking. Flip either to `Chinese` with a one-word edit if the coordinator prefers the literal report line. Cuisine counts move American 24->21, Chinese +1, Chinese-American +2. Beef Meatballs & Zoodles deliberately stays `American` — the report calls filing it under `Italian` the actual mislabel, and the zoodles have no Italian pedigree; did not upgrade it to `Italian-American` on my own judgement. No recipe in this slice hard-coded a cooking liquid volume (every starch defers to package directions) and no Water was added to any ingredients array; the only water reference is 'a splash of water' for the Beef & Broccoli slurry. Cauliflower leaves Beef Stir Fry only and Garlic Powder leaves the spice overrides of Beef Stir Fry and Beef & Broccoli — neither is orphaned, both remain in use elsewhere. No nuts, no olives, no Sumac anywhere; Pesto Sauce left untouched under the nut-free-brand rule. Macro deltas are all within the report's predictions, largest being BBQ Chicken Plate at roughly +145 cal (mayo + roasting oil), which the report explicitly justified.
